clue.text: Rev up?

parts.note: a Rev, a reverend, is someone whose work points up towards heaven: a clergyman seen as a pilot of souls in the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev up' looks like revving an engine; read it as a reverend who works 'up' above. SKY PILOT is old slang for a clergyman, especially a forces chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is slang for a chaplain or minister, and Rev abbreviates reverend.

clue.text: Stimulant drug reduced what a blow!

parts.note: an upper is slang for a stimulant drug such as amphetamine
cut means reduced, as prices are cut

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the effect of a weakened pep pill.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a boxing punch, a blow driven upward to the chin.

clue.text: Common clothes-belt

explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is informal British slang for clothes or gear, and as a verb means to hit hard, to wallop.

clue.text: Instrument for one of eight in a circle

definitions.text: one of eight in a circle

explanation.definitionFit: An octant is a navigational instrument like a sextant measuring angles, and also an eighth part of a circle, a 45-degree arc.

clue.text: High court judge?

parts.note: the court is a tennis court, and its judge sits up high in a tall chair beside the net

explanation.walkthrough: 'High court judge' suggests a senior legal figure; the court is a tennis court and the official sits on a high chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The tennis official who rules on play is seated in an elevated chair at the side of the court.

clue.text: How to get the time right on the beat?

definitions.text: How to get the time right on the beat?

parts.words: How to get the time right on the beat?
parts.note: the beat is a constable's patrol route; the old advice for finding the time was to put the question to a passing bobby

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the beat' suggests music and rhythm; here it is the patrolling police officer, whom people traditionally asked for the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase for seeking information from a constable on patrol, the traditional way to learn the hour.

clue.text: A Harrogate feature, rough sugar, ends succulent starter

parts.note: Harrogate is a Yorkshire spa town, famous for its mineral springs

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters of the word sugar are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: tips are ends, as of fingers or shoots

explanation.surface: A visitor to Harrogate describes rough sugar and a tasty first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns SUGAR into RAGUS; Harrogate is a spa town in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The tender tops of the vegetable spears are a classic juicy first course.

clue.text: One is expected to stay in as it gets dark!

definitions.text: One is expected to stay in as it gets dark!

parts.words: One is expected to stay in as it gets dark!
parts.note: in cricket a lower-order batter is sent in near close of play to survive, staying in, until stumps as light fades

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a security guard; in cricket a nightwatchman is a lesser batter sent in late in the day to protect the better ones and survive until play ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a guard who patrols after dark and the cricket batter sent in late to keep his wicket.

clue.text: Epic poem-record work needs double energy!

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
op, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: double means the abbreviation for energy is written twice in a row

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A recording of an epic poem calls for a lot of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: An epopee is an epic, a long heroic narrative verse work.

clue.text: Ship's position in rollers, perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's bearings fix its location relative to landmarks, and ball bearings are small rolling parts in machinery.

clue.text: Polish grate

explanation.definitionFit: To rub is to polish a surface, and rubbing harshly is to grate or chafe.

clue.text: For changing, 51 centigrade is a lark!

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the word for switch around

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
C is the abbreviation for centigrade

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a temperature of 51 degrees would be fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic and a lark are both bits of light-hearted fun.

clue.text: Suit England's openers packed, we hear

parts.note: the first two letters of the word England
packed sounds like pact, and a pact is a treaty

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen are said to be crammed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'packed' into its sound-alike 'pact', which then means TREATY.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is a plea or petition, as when a suitor makes a request.

clue.text: Whisky and port at one time?

explanation.definitionFit: Rye is an American grain spirit, and the Sussex town of Rye was a Cinque Port until its harbour silted up.

clue.text: It takes a crowd outside to excite trouble

indicators.note: outside, with takes, says the crowd word wraps around the word it

parts.note: a gate is the crowd attending a sports match

explanation.surface: A crowd forms and trouble breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: A GATE is the attendance at a match; it goes outside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up unrest or campaign for change.

clue.text: A jolly member

parts.note: a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is not cheerful but slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A member is a limb of the body.

clue.text: Time of graceful deliveries?

parts.note: the nursery rhyme says the child born on a certain weekday is full of grace, so births that day are graceful deliveries

explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests cricket bowling or post; it means births. The rhyme 'Monday's child' has the line 'Tuesday's child is full of grace'.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekday whose child, in the traditional rhyme, is full of grace.

clue.text: Up the creek, say, and against the current

explanation.definitionFit: Going up a creek is heading towards its source, and that direction runs against the flow of water.

clue.text: Harem women in Sligo are unusual

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of Sligo and are form an odd new arrangement

explanation.surface: A harem in the Irish town of Sligo would be a rare thing.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIGO + ARE is rearranged; Sligo is a town in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Turkish palace, and by extension the concubines living there.

clue.text: Estate needs me in management

indicators.note: management, handling things, signals the letters of needs and me are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone running a property says it can't manage without them.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land attached to a manor and kept for the owner's own use.

clue.text: Tea-time's difficult to guess

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters of tea-time's are knotted into a new order

parts.note: the letters of tea-time's including the s

explanation.surface: It is hard to say when tea will be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges TEATIMES; the 's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge roughly, to make an approximate reckoning.

clue.text: Doing time? That's confidential

explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for being in prison, and inside information is private, known only to insiders.

clue.text: A fellow not convincing when aroused

parts.note: a lame excuse is one that does not convince

explanation.surface: A man is unpersuasive when his passions are stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aflame is burning with passion or excitement.

clue.text: Trim conifer

explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and smart in appearance, and the spruce is an evergreen fir-like tree.

clue.text: Having toughened surface where wrestler falls

explanation.definitionFit: Mat describes a dull, frosted finish like matt glass, and a wrestling bout is fought on a padded floor covering.

clue.text: Break up Norfolk town with unbridled love

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, England

indicators.note: unbridled, let loose, signals the letters of love are freed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Norfolk town is the scene of passionate romance.
explanation.walkthrough: DISS is a small market town in Norfolk; 'unbridled' rearranges LOVE into OLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve a partnership or parliament is to end it, to break it up.

clue.text: Course of therapy for most of the army unit

indicators.note: most of says the army word loses its last letters

parts.note: a regiment is a unit of the army

explanation.surface: A soldier's battalion is put on a treatment plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime, like a regimen, is a prescribed plan of diet or treatment.

clue.text: Meditate on sin, perhaps, in this settlement?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of meditate on sin might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A monk ponders sin in a quiet community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MEDITATE ON SIN; 'settlement' is not a village but the sinking of particles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedimentation is the settling of solid particles out of a liquid.
